title: ADR
oneLine: An Architecture Decision Record — one cross-cutting decision, recorded as an ordinary Library artifact of kind `adr` (id `adr-NNNN`).

title: approval
oneLine: A first-class, typed operator act (actor = operator) in which the human accepts an agent action, or a capability's green result, onto the trunk via the studio.

title: approval event / promotion event
oneLine: Typed operator-actor events in the event store: an approval / steering event (a human in-loop intervention) and a signed promotion event (the human accepting a unit's green result onto the trunk).

title: arc / epic
oneLine: The initiative overlay: a named multi-story owner intent tracked through an increment log to a closed end-state — upstream of stories and ADRs by provenance, holding its increments, rendered as "Epic" in the studio.

title: asset
oneLine: In storytree, a tree/game art asset for the isometric renderer (ADR-0001, deferred).

title: boundary
oneLine: The declared, documented seam between two stories — the only legal cross-story coupling, the way a frontend depends on a database.

title: capability
oneLine: An organ within a story (bounded context): independently viable, proven by integration tests against real in-story collaborators, and composed of contracts.

title: chip
oneLine: A one-click offer of a follow-up session, minted with `spawn_task` — where the owner's click is CONSENT to the spend and never SELECTION of the work, so the judgment of whether the work is worth doing sits entirely on the minting side.

title: claim
oneLine: A typed write-ownership record in the one shared event store, naming what a node intends to write and checked under a serializable/unique constraint at node-schedule time — a conflict is a hard refusal, never a warning.

title: consuming surface
oneLine: A consuming sink at the top of the dependency order — an app or the public subrepo — that wires organisms together and is itself depended on by nothing, yet is a first-class, enforced node in the boundary graph, not an exempt wiring layer.

title: contract
oneLine: A single test-proven behaviour within a capability — the leaf of the proof ladder, proven by one automated, isolated unit test (collaborators stubbed).

title: contract test
oneLine: The automated test that proves a contract — the isolated unit test at the bottom rung of the proof ladder (unit → integration → UAT).

title: convergence
oneLine: A term carrying two distinct senses that storytree 0.1 conflated and 0.2 keeps separate — DAG-stabilisation and cold-rebuild — so it must always be qualified.

title: DAG
oneLine: The directed acyclic graph the studio renders and watches grow — stories as visible nodes, capability dependencies as the fine-grained edges beneath.

title: dependency
oneLine: A directed edge between units, defined at two altitudes: code-derived capability→capability edges within a story, and declared boundaries across stories (ADR-0010).

title: drive
oneLine: To take a unit of decided work and carry it all the way to LANDED — decompose it, prove it red→green, gate it, open the PR, close it out — as opposed to planning it, scoping it, or exploring it.

title: event
oneLine: A typed record of a state change (owned-loop events plus orchestrator events) — the unit of observability.

title: event log
oneLine: The typed, append-only record in the event store — one row per state change — that is the single source of truth the studio renders and the only thing written.

title: evidence
oneLine: The forensic record that a unit's tests went red→green and its story's UAT was signed — an audit trail, not itself the gate.

title: fixture
oneLine: A test-supporting artifact (data file, scaffold, temp crate) created during a walkthrough and cleaned up before signing.

title: friction
oneLine: A captured, evidence-bearing record of what fought a session and at what cost — filed at most THREE per session, distilled rather than raw, and routed later rather than adjudicated at capture.

title: gate
oneLine: A structural enforcement point that refuses invalid work rather than warning about it.

title: glue
oneLine: Un-asserted code within a story: connective tissue binding proven capabilities into a running whole. It declares no capability of its own (no isolatable red→green contract) and is proven transitively at the story / UAT altitude or by operator attestation — never by its own contract.

title: Grow · Tell · Roam · Ask — the four movements of chapter 2
oneLine: The four movements of the public site's chapter 2, named so that each name states WHO IS DRIVING it: the system GROWS the forest, we TELL, the visitor ROAMS, and we ASK.

title: in-session subagent
oneLine: A subagent spawned in-process by a running session's own Agent tool — starts immediately with no owner approval, is a CHILD of the spawning session, and dies if the parent's process exits.

title: increment
oneLine: One decided-but-not-yet-built unit of work parked on an arc, carrying its own lifecycle (`proposal → ready → active → closed`) — and, once closed, the arc's permanent log entry.

title: inert
oneLine: A session that has landed and will open no new work — no monitors, no polling loops, no scheduled wakeups — reached only for one of four NAMED reasons, and never mute.

title: land / landing
oneLine: Merged to `main` — the ordinary industry sense — plus the three parts a reader does NOT already carry: CI performs the merge from a NON-DRAFT PR and the session never runs `gh pr merge`; the CLOSING LEG is part of landing, not after it (residue on the arc, claims released, owner debriefed); and an ESCALATION is also a landing, never a wait.

title: lane
oneLine: One independently-drivable strand of an arc — work whose OWN dependency sentence says nothing outstanding blocks it, so it can run beside its siblings rather than after them.

title: leaf step / leaf judgment
oneLine: A single step in a code-sequenced cascade whose work is owned by the leaf runtime (what to write, how to satisfy a contract) rather than by the spine — the control-flow sense of "leaf".

title: library
oneLine: The shared **knowledge tier**: schema-validated artifact docs — reference (definitions, techstack), behavioural rules (principles, guardrails, patterns), ways-of-working (processes), roles (agents), initiative overlays (arcs), and transient signal units (open questions, friction, resteer) — living in the shared Cloud SQL Postgres store, read just-in-time by sessions through the CLI and by humans through the studio.

title: lifecycle status
oneLine: A unit's status, drawn from six states — proposed, building, healthy, unhealthy, mapped, retired — that track it from authoring through proven to pruned.

title: MAST failure frame
oneLine: The ADOPTED (never invented) vocabulary for classifying one agent failure or one owner re-steer: MAST's 14 modes in three categories, plus the four measured storytree extension modes in their own category, plus exactly one escape hatch, `no-mast-home`, whose use is a finding rather than a cop-out.

title: mock-UAT seam
oneLine: The rule that there are no mocks within an organism — capability integration tests and the story UAT both run against real in-story collaborators — with the sole stubbable boundary being the declared cross-story boundary.

title: ndjson
oneLine: Newline-delimited JSON — the line-delimited record format (a candidate backing for the event stream).

title: node / storynode
oneLine: A unit being worked on the DAG — a story or capability under construction — driven by one owned-loop session (the intended DBOS workflow wrapper is deferred, ADR-0019).

title: node rollup
oneLine: The current status and latest verdict per story / capability / contract, derived as a projection over the event log and never hand-maintained.

title: noticeboard
oneLine: The claim ledger — one of the three working surfaces (tree = the work, **noticeboard** = the sessions, library = the knowledge): sessions are forced to claim their unit at start (the capability being written, ADR-0270 D1; the story for cross-capability work), and coordination + observability are two views over ONE deterministic ledger (grades: exploring / waiting / work). The old advisory, staleness-aged session-presence rows are retired (ADR-0200).

title: operator-attested
oneLine: A proof mode for behavioural/guardrail surfaces with neither an honest scripted UAT nor an isolatable automated test, where promotion to `healthy` is an explicit, per-unit, operator-granted signed event.

title: orchestrator
oneLine: The thin custom TypeScript layer (`packages/orchestrator`) over plain Postgres (DBOS deferred, ADR-0019) that owns the story-DAG, the scheduler, and the event store, and is the only module that drives `packages/agent` (the owned loop).

title: per-node budget
oneLine: A code-enforced ceiling on a node's spine loop that bounds a runaway. On a `--real` build the brake is the build's wall-clock time budget (default two hours, ADR-0581/ADR-0584); the turn cap (`maxTurns`) remains the brake wherever no budget is wired (`--live`, `--dry-run`). The USD ceiling was dropped as a default — a phantom under subscription billing — and is now an opt-in `--budget` escape hatch (ADR-0130/0131).

title: agent package
oneLine: The project-owned packages/agent boundary around every model harness, exposing only runtime-neutral authoring and typed accounting upward.

title: owned-loop event stream
oneLine: The owned loop's structured lifecycle event stream (plus edit-tool diffs) emitted as it works inside a node — the agent-activity ingest channel into the event store, normalized by packages/agent.

title: Plan
oneLine: One unit of arc work, from decided to landed: the units in dependency order with their proof routes, contention, budgets and traps, written as one free `body` — freshness-checked at consumption, executed once, then closed. The KIND is `increment` (ADR-0305 D1).

title: probe
oneLine: A **probe** is the owner's working term (alias) for an **explorer subagent**: a read-only, disposable subagent sent out to answer one scoped question — find, verify, survey — and return a DIGEST (conclusions plus file:line pointers), never raw file dumps.

title: proof hash
oneLine: A hash of a unit's proof-bearing content (outcome, contracts, …) that invalidates a prior verdict when the content changes.

title: Proof mode
oneLine: The four ways a unit earns `healthy` — one rung per tier — comprising UAT, integration-test, contract-test, and operator-attested.

title: reonboard
oneLine: To bring the owner back up to speed when he re-enters a thread cold — where things STAND, what he needs to KNOW to follow it, what you MAKE of it, what you WANT from him — offered unprompted, because being asked for it is the failure signal.

title: residue
oneLine: What a session writes onto the owning arc when it ends — what it attempted, what landed, what did not, and what the next session needs in order to resume — and it is the handover, because there is no other.

title: run
oneLine: A single per-node execution attempt, recorded as an event in the event store — many-per-node, never a new node.

title: self-perpetuating session
oneLine: A session that supplies its own continuation rather than waiting for the owner to supply it: it takes the next work when it lands, and when a real end forces it out it cuts its OWN successor rather than leaving the owner a click.

title: session cutting / cut a fresh session
oneLine: The owner-approved delegation mechanism — a fresh top-level Claude Code session (own context, lifecycle, SessionStart hooks) launched via the desktop's `spawn_task` chip, surviving the proposing session entirely.

title: software factory
oneLine: A delivery loop whose output includes a revision of its own operating instructions — storytree's whole cycle from owner intent to landed code, named for the return edge that makes it self-retooling rather than merely repeatable.

title: spine
oneLine: The code-sequenced control-flow layer (the orchestrator over plain Postgres, DBOS deferred — ADR-0019) that owns closed, deterministic routing — the order steps run in, when a loop iterates, which branch is taken.

title: steering
oneLine: A first-class, typed operator act of redirecting an in-flight owned-loop run mid-execution (the owned loop's `steer` operation), recorded as an event in the event store.

title: story
oneLine: The top-level unit of work you watch grow — a bounded context / organism, self-contained and independently deployable, composed of capabilities and proven as a whole by integrated UAT.

title: story tree
oneLine: The work surface: the living, populated DAG of stories > capabilities > contracts along which the software is grown — authored as files under `stories/`, rendered by the storytree CLI and the studio, and watched by a human as the map of the AI-driven SDLC.

title: studio
oneLine: The live PixiJS web IDE that renders the tree and drives the agents — diffs, approvals, steering, per-node chat.

title: trunk
oneLine: The canonical integrated mainline a capability lands on once approved.

title: UAT
oneLine: A prose journey, run end-to-end against real collaborators, that proves a story (the whole organism) meets its goal.

title: unit fields
oneLine: The four core fields a unit carries — outcome, guidance, title, id — covering its value statement, rebuild context, human label, and unique identifier.

title: verdict
oneLine: The Pass/Fail outcome of a story's UAT.

title: work hierarchy is disk-canonical
oneLine: The work hierarchy (story / capability / contract) lives as frontmatter-markdown files under stories/ — disk-canonical, landed via the PR — while the knowledge tier lives in the live --pg store; author each tier on its own canonical surface.

title: worktree
oneLine: A git-registered linked checkout that is ALSO the session's identity — which is why the primary checkout is deliberately refused one, and why a session without a worktree can claim nothing.

title: write-ownership
oneLine: The single vocabulary for what surface/unit a node claims the right to write, used by the claim / conflict-detection layer.
